mstts:express-as.prosody: Welcome to this journey where we’re going to explore the ways power can quietly undermine the very foundations it promises to protect. Have you ever wondered how even the strongest democracies might start to unravel from within? That’s exactly the kind of question Noam Chomsky invites us to consider in his thought-provoking book, Failed States: The Abuse of Power and the Assault on Democracy. Here, the idea of a “failed state” isn’t just about faraway, unstable nations. Instead, we’ll see how the world’s most influential countries can, sometimes without us noticing, erode their own democratic values—by shaping opinions, dodging accountability, and putting their own interests ahead of the people they’re meant to serve. Together, we’ll dig into the ripple effects of these choices, both at home and on the global stage. You’ll find out how foreign policy, economics, and our basic freedoms are all deeply connected—and how, when power goes unchecked, it can threaten justice and real participation for everyone. Chomsky’s work challenges us to question what we think we know about national greatness and reminds us why transparency, vigilance, and genuine engagement matter so much. So, as we set out on this exploration, let’s stay curious and open, ready to better understand what’s at stake when societies drift away from the core values of democracy. There’s a lot to uncover about the forces shaping our shared future, and I’m glad we’re diving in together.
